claims.statement: The worker process builds its own svcs DI registry: `setup_worker_services` (`@huey.on_startup()`) calls `init_logging()`, registers huey-dashboard signals via `init_worker_signals`, creates a dedicated `DatabaseSessionManager` using `NullPool`, registers the service graph on a fresh `Registry`, and assigns it to `huey.svcs_registry`; `@huey.on_shutdown()` closes that registry. NullPool is required because each task invocation calls `asyncio.run()`, and a pooled async engine reused across those short-lived event loops raises "operation in progress" errors.

`src/worker.py` selects the Huey implementation by environment — `MemoryHueyWithRegistry` when `settings.environment == "test"`, otherwise `RedisHueyWithRegistry` bound to `settings.redis_url` — and imports `src.account.task`, `src.integration.task` and `src.market.task` at the bottom of the module purely so their decorators register against the same `huey` instance.

Task bodies split into two guard styles against a missing worker registry: `_daily_price_update`, `_hourly_intraday_price_update`, `_recalculate_all_account_totals` and `_sync_account_positions_task` raise `RuntimeError("Worker registry not initialized")`, while `_generate_note_title`, `_check_and_dispatch_price_alerts` and `_alert_email_dispatch` return early. Every task body is a thin synchronous wrapper over `asyncio.run(<async impl>)`, and the tasks accepting a `request_id` (`sync_account_positions_task`, `generate_note_title_task`) set and then reset the request-id contextvar in a `finally`.

Stage 1 of the price cascade — `_hourly_intraday_price_update` — runs `MarketService.update_intraday_prices_for_all_securities`, logs `success`/`failure` counts, and then performs two independently-guarded enqueues of `recalculate_all_account_totals_task` and `check_and_dispatch_price_alerts`, each wrapped in its own `try/except` that only calls `logger.exception`; a failure of either enqueue does not prevent the other from being enqueued and does not propagate out of the periodic task.

`alert_email_dispatch_task` is the only task declaring `retries=3`, and it delegates to `AlertEvaluationService.dispatch_alert_email`, which implements email-then-mark: it no-ops when the alert is gone or already has `triggered_at`, re-resolves the latest intraday price at dispatch time, sends the email, and only then calls `mark_triggered(alert_id, run_ts)`; a send failure is logged and re-raised so Huey retries while `triggered_at` stays NULL for the next hourly Stage 2 re-enqueue.

`sync_account_positions_task` is enqueued synchronously from the request path — by `POST /api/v1/accounts/{account_id}/sync` (rate-limited `3/minute`) through `PositionService.sync_account_positions` → `IntegrationAccountApi.sync_account_positions`, which forwards `get_request_id()` — and once per newly imported broker account in the broker import route.

One account sync follows a fixed order: `mark_sync_started` in its own log-only `try/except` that must not abort a healthy sync on a Redis outage; publish `sync_started`; run `_do_sync_positions`; publish `sync_finished`; on any exception log, attempt `_send_sync_error_email` inside its own `try/except` so a mail failure is swallowed, publish `sync_failed`, and re-raise so Huey records the failure; `mark_sync_finished` runs in a `finally` so it executes on success, failure and re-raise alike.

A `@huey.signal(signals.SIGNAL_INTERRUPTED)` handler in `src/integration/task.py` guards specifically on `task.name == "sync_account_positions_task"`, reads `task.args[0]`/`task.args[1]` and calls `mark_sync_finished` via `asyncio.run`, so a killed worker does not leave an account stuck in the syncing set until the TTL expires.

`ws_manager = ConnectionManager()` is a process-global singleton holding `active_connections: dict[UserId, list[WebSocket]]` and a per-event-loop Redis client map `_clients: dict[asyncio.AbstractEventLoop, aioredis.Redis]` guarded by a `threading.Lock`, plus a single `_pubsub_task`. `get_redis_client()` returns the client for the currently running loop or `None` with no running loop; `init_redis(redis_url, run_listener=True)` prunes and `aclose()`s clients whose loop has closed, lazily creates a `decode_responses=True` client for the current loop, and starts the listener only when none is live. `tests/tasks/test_redis_concurrency.py` pins the two-threads/two-loops isolation, closed-loop pruning and orphan `aclose()`.

`send_personal_message` resolves the current loop's Redis client, lazily calling `init_redis(settings.redis_url, run_listener=False)` (a publish-only client, never a subscriber) when none exists, publishes `json.dumps({"user_id": str(user_id), "message": message})` to the `ws_messages` channel, and falls back to `_send_to_local_connections` when init fails or the publish raises — so a Redis outage degrades to same-process delivery instead of dropping the event. `send_personal_message_sync` schedules the coroutine on the running loop or falls back to `asyncio.run`.

`_listen_for_messages` subscribes to `ws_messages`, decodes each payload, coerces `user_id` back to a `UUID` and calls `_send_to_local_connections`, which skips sockets whose `client_state` is not `WebSocketState.CONNECTED` and logs without aborting the batch on a per-socket send failure; a malformed payload is logged and the loop continues, `CancelledError` unsubscribes and closes the pubsub, and any other exception logs, sleeps 5 seconds and starts a fresh listener task.

`lifespan_context` in `src/main.py` calls `await ws_manager.init_redis(settings.redis_url)` at startup so the API's main loop owns the pub/sub listener, and on shutdown calls `close_worker_dashboard(app)`, `await ws_manager.close()` and `await redis_manager.close()`; `ws_router` is included outside the `/api/v1` prefix so the endpoint is `/api/ws`.

`POST /api/v1/auth/ws-ticket` requires the `auth_token` cookie (else 401), resolves the user through `UserApi.get_current_user_from_token`, and returns `URLSafeTimedSerializer(settings.secret_key).dumps(json.dumps({"user_id": ..., "jti": ...}), salt="ws-ticket")` — the short-lived ticket the frontend uses instead of putting the session token in a WebSocket URL.

`GET /api/ws` accepts two credential shapes: a `?ticket=` query param validated by `_check_ticket_not_replayed` followed by `serializer.loads(ticket, max_age=30, salt="ws-ticket")`, or the `auth_token` cookie / `sec-websocket-protocol` header resolved through `UserApi.get_current_user_from_token` inside `svcs.Container(websocket.app.state.svcs_registry)`. On success it negotiates `subprotocol = token if sec-websocket-protocol else None`, calls `ws_manager.connect`, and loops on `receive_text()` until `WebSocketDisconnect` triggers `ws_manager.disconnect`; the endpoint installs a request id from `X-Request-ID` or a fresh `uuid4()` and resets the contextvar in a `finally`.

The ticket replay guard `_check_ticket_not_replayed` computes `sha256(ticket)`, runs `SET ws-ticket-used:<hash> "1" NX EX 30` on a short-lived client, and returns False when the key already existed (the caller then closes with code 1008); on a Redis exception it logs and returns True, i.e. it fails open so a Redis outage silently disables replay protection rather than locking users out.

Every other authentication outcome on `/api/ws` also closes the connection with WebSocket policy-violation code 1008 — a replayed ticket, an unparsable or expired ticket, a token that fails verification, or no credential at all — as pinned by `tests/ws/test_router.py`.

`src/integration/sync_status.py` owns one key shape, `account_syncs:active:{user_id}`, and three operations through the per-loop `redis_manager.client()` context manager: `mark_sync_started` does `SADD` then `EXPIRE ... settings.sync_ttl_seconds`, `mark_sync_finished` does `SREM`, and `get_active_syncs` does `SMEMBERS` returning UUIDs. `sync_ttl_seconds` defaults to 300 and is the safety net for a worker dying without cleanup; the set is display state, not a lock, so concurrent syncs of one account collapse to one member and the first `SREM` clears the badge.

`GET /api/v1/accounts/sync-status` sits behind `current_user`, returns `{"account_ids": [str(id), ...]}` scoped to the caller, and translates `redis.RedisError` into 503 `"Sync status service unavailable"`; `tests/routers/test_sync_status.py` pins the empty result, the per-user scoping, the unauthenticated 401/403 and the Redis-down 503.

`src/core/redis.py` provides `RedisManager`, the per-event-loop Redis client owner used by the sync-status path (distinct from the WebSocket manager's private client map): `client()` is an async context manager that prunes clients whose loop has closed, awaits `aclose()` on them, and lazily creates a `decode_responses=True` client for the running loop. `redis_manager = RedisManager(settings.redis_url)` is the shared singleton, and `tests/tasks/test_redis_concurrency.py` exercises this manager with the same two-threads/two-loops pattern as `ConnectionManager`.

`AccountsListState` (`frontend/src/lib/components/accounts/accounts-list.svelte.ts`) is the only browser-side WebSocket consumer. Its constructor calls `initWebSocket()` when `browser` is true; the URL is derived from `VITE_API_BASE_URL` when it starts with `http` (mapping `https`→`wss:`, stripping the scheme, taking the first host segment and appending `/api/ws`), otherwise from `window.location`; it obtains a ticket via `authService.getWsTicket()` mapping the response to `data?.ticket ?? null` and catching rejections to `null`, and when no ticket is obtained it logs a warning and returns **without connecting** — there is no unauthenticated attempt and no retry for that failure. On success it opens ``new WebSocket(`${wsUrl}?ticket=${encodeURIComponent(ticket)}`)``.

The frontend's `onopen` sets `wsConnected = true` and calls `hydrateSyncStatus()`, which issues one `GET /accounts/sync-status` and adds every returned id to `syncingAccountIds`, guarded by the `syncStatusHydrated` flag so a single connection lifetime polls only once; a failed hydration is logged and leaves the flag unset so it is retried on the next open. `wsConnected` drives the Live/Disconnected dot in `accounts-list.svelte`.

The frontend `onmessage` handler switches on `data.type`: `sync_started` adds the id to `syncingAccountIds` and sets `syncErrors[id] = null`; `sync_finished` removes the id, clears the error, and **awaits `fetchAccounts()`** to pick up the new positions; `sync_failed` removes the id and sets `'Failed to sync. Please try again.'`. A parse failure is caught and logged without touching state. `frontend/src/lib/types/websocket.ts` declares only those three event values, so the backend's fourth event `account_totals_updated` matches no branch and changes no state in this component.

The frontend `onclose` handler sets `wsConnected = false`, resets `syncStatusHydrated = false` so the next open re-hydrates, and re-invokes `initWebSocket()` after a fixed 5000 ms `setTimeout` (fetching a fresh ticket on every attempt); `destroy()` closes the socket and nulls the reference.

`waitForSyncFinish(id)` is the frontend's socket-independent fallback: it polls `GET /accounts/sync-status` every 1500 ms against a 60000 ms deadline, waits a 5000 ms grace period once the backend stops reporting the id, then clears `syncingAccountIds`, clears the error and refetches accounts if the WS message never arrived; a status-endpoint failure is swallowed and the loop keeps waiting, and on deadline it clears the id and sets `'Sync took too long. Check account status.'`. `syncAccount(id)` also clears the id and sets `'Request failed. Please check your connection.'` when the POST itself fails.

`worker_dashboard_router = APIRouter(prefix="/worker/api")` mounts huey-dashboard's task router under `/tasks` with `dependencies=[Depends(current_user)]`, exposing authenticated `GET /worker/api/tasks/` and `GET /worker/api/tasks/{task_id}`; `tests/routers/test_worker_dashboard.py` asserts 401 without credentials and 200/404 with them.

The dashboard's live-updates WebSocket at `/worker/api/updates` (and `/worker/api/updates/`) reuses the same two credential shapes as `/api/ws` — a signed ticket validated by `_check_ticket_not_replayed` imported from `src.ws.router` plus `serializer.loads(..., max_age=30, salt="ws-ticket")`, or the `auth_token` cookie / `sec-websocket-protocol` token resolved through `UserApi` — and closes with code 1008 on any failure. On success it accepts the socket (passing the token as the negotiated subprotocol when the client requested one, otherwise plain `manager.connect`), echoes `Message received: <data>` for each inbound text frame until `WebSocketDisconnect` calls `manager.disconnect`, and installs the same `X-Request-ID`-or-`uuid4()` request id reset in a `finally`.

`init_worker_dashboard` (`src/worker_dashboard/setup.py`) creates an async engine and a huey-dashboard `TaskDatabase`, calls `db.ensure_table()`, stores `{"huey", "redis", "manager", "db"}` on `app.state.huey_dashboard`, optionally registers the dashboard signal handlers against the running loop when `bind_signals=True`, and starts the dashboard's Redis pub/sub listener; `close_worker_dashboard` stops the listener and closes the Redis client. The FastAPI lifespan calls the former at startup and the latter on shutdown, and the worker side feeds the dashboard through `init_worker_signals(huey=huey, db_url=..., redis_url=...)`.

The dev `worker` service runs `huey_consumer src.worker.huey -w 2 --worker-type thread --periodic` (wrapped in `watchfiles`) with `HUEY_DASHBOARD_WORKER: 1`, while `docker-compose.prod.yml` runs the same consumer command **without** `--periodic`. Without that flag Huey ignores `crontab` schedules entirely and periodic tasks never fire — the regression pinned by `test_worker_command_enables_periodic_scheduling`, which reads `docker-compose.yml` and asserts both `huey_consumer` and `--periodic` are present.

The test suite never requires a live Redis, a running worker or a real socket: `tests/conftest.py` sets `huey.immediate = True`, patches `ConnectionManager.init_redis`, `close`, `send_personal_message` and `send_personal_message_sync` at class level so every loop-scoped instance is inert, and patches `src.main.init_worker_dashboard`/`src.main.close_worker_dashboard` where `main.py` bound them to avoid real `AsyncRedis` teardown (~4 s per test); the autouse `fake_redis_manager` fixture swaps `src.core.redis.redis_manager.client` for a dict-backed `FakeRedis` implementing `set(nx=...)`, `sadd`/`srem`/`smembers`, `expire`, `publish` and `aclose`.

`GET /health/ready` in `src/main.py` pings Redis through `redis_manager.client()`, so a Redis outage degrades the readiness probe in addition to the WebSocket fan-out and the account-sync status endpoint.
